analyzed_vuln.description: In `dissect_softether_host_fqdn`, the code copies `val1.value_size` bytes from `val1.value.ptr.value_str` using `strncpy` after only checking `val1.type == VALUE_STR && val1.value_size > 0`. It does not verify that `val1.value_size` is actually within the remaining packet buffer for that parsed value. A malformed SoftEther tuple can therefore produce a VALUE_STR with an oversized length, causing `strncpy` to read past valid packet data into ASan-poisoned memory (use-after-poison read). The crash occurs at the `strncpy` into `flow->protos.softether.fqdn` (and similarly possible for hostname).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Via `fuzz_process_packet`, attacker-controlled packet bytes reach `ndpi_detection_process_packet` and then `ndpi_search_softether`, which calls `dissect_softether_host_fqdn` for payloads >=99 bytes. The input must parse enough to set `got_fqdn`/`got_hostname` and produce a `val1` tuple marked as VALUE_STR with positive but inconsistent/too-large `value_size`, so `len = min(val1.value_size, dst_size-1)` remains nonzero while source bytes are not fully available. Then `strncpy(..., val1.value.ptr.value_str, len)` performs an out-of-bounds read from poisoned region, triggering the reported ASan error.
